subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server TCP and Unix WebSocket opening handshakes fail after 30 seconds with the proposed error and abnormal-close semantics?
rationale: The patch fixes a demonstrated indefinite wait, but selecting a hard timeout and terminal-event contract changes existing connection behavior and is an owner-level compatibility decision.

options.title: Accept the 30-second boundary
options.body: Land the current transport-level timeout and documented error/exit behavior as the supported failure policy for stalled upgrades.

options.title: Revise the timeout contract
options.body: Choose a different fixed duration or terminal-event precedence, then update the focused tests and real-socket proof to match.

options.title: Keep unlimited waiting
options.body: Decline the behavioral change and accept that stalled peers can leave initialization and queued RPC frames pending indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second boundary
recommendation.body: Land the current transport-level timeout and documented error/exit behavior as the supported failure policy for stalled upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history places this person closest to recent Codex app-server runtime and liveness decisions.
